newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik group threatens to kill UN hostages.
newsitem.headline: Tajik group threatens to kill UN hostages.

text.p: A group of unidentified armed men seized 15 hostages, including eight foreign United Nations military observers, in Tajikistan on Friday and threatened to shoot them if their demands were not met in two days.

A U.N. source in the capital Dushanbe told Reuters the group seized a five-vehicle column carrying 11 U.N. personnel and four representatives of the country's armed Islamic opposition and demanded that the rebels free the brother of an opposition chief who joined forces with the government last month.
If their demands were not met by 2 p.m. (0900 GMT) on Sunday, they said, they would shoot the hostages and detonate 30 bombs, which had been secreted around Dushanbe.

The incident happened as Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and exiled opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri were in Moscow for talks on ending the bloody four-year civil war in the former Soviet republic. The two men met briefly on Thursday. Officials from the two sides held a second day of discussions on Friday.
It was not clear how many hostage-takers there were nor who they were. But their demands suggested they were fighters loyal to the guerrilla commander who had switched sides.

Their second key condition for releasing the hostages was that Russian border guards, thousands of whom who have been acting as peacekeepers, provide safe passage for fighters loyal to the defecting leader to join them from their bases across the Afghan border.

The incident happened about 70 km (40 miles) east of Dushanbe as the U.N. convoy was travelling from the city of Garm, in central Tajikistan, where government troops and opposition forces have clashed recently.

Information on the nationalities of the eight foreign hostages was not immediately available. There were three Tajik members of the 11-strong U.N. team. The U.N. mission to Tajikistan fields 96 foreign military observers in the republic and had its mandate renewed for four months last week.
The observers have already twice this month been subject to beatings and mock executions. The two earlier incidents were at the hands of Tajik government soldiers.
